terms.comment: The Arabian Gulf, the Romans’ name for what we call the Red Sea; their mare Rubrum was a wider sea, taking in the Persian Gulf and the Indian Ocean (M-O).

evidence: Vulg. Exod. 13.18: per viam dēsertī quae est juxtā mare Rubrum
Tac. A. 14.25: ad lītora maris Rubrī
M-O s.v. seas: Red Sea (Trappen, 1843; Egger)
terms.comment: The usual name today. Classically mare Rubrum was the wider sea east of Arabia (M-O), as in Nepos’ usque ā rubrō marī (Hann. 2.1, Lewis & Short s.v. usque) and in Tacitus; the Vulgate gives it to the sea of the Exodus, the Red Sea proper, and so it is labelled late in this sense.

sources: Lewis & Short: ruber
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. seas: Red Sea.
